name: Question 2
problem: Find the surface area of the portion of the cone $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ that is bounded by the constraints $0\le x\le 1$ and $1\le y\le 2.$
worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},\,0\le x\le 1,\,1\le y\le 2.
$$

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})^{2}+(\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+1}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{2}{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot (1-0)\cdot (2-1) \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For a surface S defined by z=f(x,y) with (x,y)∈D, the surface area of S is given by ∬SdS=∬D1+(∂z∂x)2+(∂z∂y)2dA.

In this case, our surface is given by z=x2+y2,0≤x≤1,1≤y≤2.

Now, since ∂z∂x=∂∂x(x2+y2)=xx2+y2,∂z∂y=∂∂y(x2+y2)=yx2+y2,

the surface area is given by ∬SdS=∬D1+(∂z∂x)2+(∂z∂y)2dA=∬D1+(xx2+y2)2+(yx2+y2)2dA=∬D1+x2x2+y2+y2x2+y2dA=∬D1+x2+y2x2+y2dA=∬D1+1dA=∬D2dA=2∬DdA=2⋅(1−0)⋅(2−1)=2.
